title: Henry 2003: twenty goals, twenty assists, no Ballon d'Or
checked: Henry 2002-03: 24 PL goals, 20 PL assists (record then), PFA and FWA awards (FourFourTwo, Squawka, Wikipedia); 2003 vote Nedved 190, Henry 128, Maldini 123 (UEFA, Topend, Maxifoot 62-point gap); Juve won 2002-03 Serie A, Nedved suspended for the final after a yellow in the Real Madrid semi, Milan won on penalties after 0-0 at Old Trafford (Wikipedia Juve season, Forza Italian Football, UEFA); 2003-04 unbeaten 38 games, Henry 30 league goals (Premier League, FourFourTwo); 2004 Shevchenko 175, Deco 139, Ronaldinho 133, Henry 4th on 80 (Wikipedia, CBC). Picked 2003: he was second, 62 points back; in 2004 he was only fourth, 95 back. Football365's 'myth' argument is mentioned for balance.

lines.text: Twenty-four goals. Twenty assists. And Thierry Henry still didn't win the Ballon d'Or.
Twenty-oh-two oh-three. Henry was scoring them and making them.
Twenty assists was a Premier League record at the time.
He swept the PFA and the Football Writers' awards.
In Turin, Pavel Nedvěd drove Juventus to the Serie A title and the Champions League final.
Then a yellow card in the semi against Real Madrid. Suspended. He missed the final.
Without him, Juve drew nil-nil with Milan and lost on penalties.
Nedvěd one hundred and ninety points. Henry one hundred and twenty-eight. Not even close.
Some writers call the Henry robbery a myth. Nedvěd was brilliant too.

scene.heading: THE OTHER SIDE
scene.body: Nedvěd won Serie A and carried Juventus to a Champions League final. Some writers argue the Henry robbery is a football myth.

lines.text: Next season, Arsenal went the whole league unbeaten. Henry scored thirty.
And he finished fourth. Shevchenko won it.
So which year was the real robbery? Twenty-oh-three. Second place, the best season of his life, and the winner missed the final.
